paragraph_preview: Commercial and Agronomic Master Database of the Edible and Agricultural Biodiversity of North-East India
Geographic and Economic Framework for Procurement Mapping

The North-East Region (NER) of India—comprising the states of Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, and Tripura—is a vital reservoir of rare flora, fauna, and indigenous agricultural systems 1 . Characterised by extreme altitudinal gradients ranging from 300 to over 3,000 metres above mean sea level, the region spans microclimates from humid subtropical plains to alpine zones 3 . This complex geography, combined with highly acidic clay-loam soils ( ), has fostered a dense concentration of endemic plant and animal species 2 . Traditional farming communities have domesticatied and preserved these genetic resources over centuries 1 .

The Geographical Indications of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act, 1999, serves as the primary legal framework to protect the intellectual property of these unique regional goods 8 . Administered by the Geographical Indications Registry in Chennai, a Geographical Indication (GI) tag guarantees origin, standardises quality, and prevents unauthorized commercial exploitation by third parties 10 . In the NER, where agricultural systems are organic by default, GI tagging acts as a commercial catalyst 7 . It transitions subsistence crops into high-value export commodities, enabling local Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs) and tribal cooperatives to command premium pricing in domestic and international wellness markets 14 .

This master database has been compiled to serve as an exhaustive reference for NE Harvest, procurement mapping, FPO onboarding, export planning, product cataloguing, and value-added processing identification. It maps the regional edible biodiversity of the NER across 15 distinct product categories, detailing state-wise distribution, commercial potential, and legal status.
